questions.question: Which of the following is true about the relationship between lattice points and unit cells?

answers.a: Each lattice point represents an individual atom or molecule.
answers.b: A unit cell can contain multiple lattice points.
answers.c: Lattice points are only located at the corners of unit cells.
answers.d: The number of lattice points in a unit cell is always equal to one.

explanations.b: A unit cell can contain multiple lattice points, especially in non-primitive cells where points may be located at corners, faces, or within the cell.

questions.question: In a body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, where are the lattice points located?

answers.b: At the corners and the center of each face.
answers.c: At the corners and the center of the cell.
answers.d: At the center of each edge.

explanations.c: In a BCC lattice, lattice points are located at each corner and a single point at the center of the unit cell.

questions.question: How does the choice of unit cell affect the calculated density of a crystal?

answers.a: The choice of unit cell does not affect the calculated density.
answers.b: Using a non-primitive unit cell will result in a higher calculated density.
answers.c: Using a primitive unit cell will result in a higher calculated density.
answers.d: The calculated density is only accurate when using the smallest possible unit cell.

explanations.a: The calculated density of a crystal is an intrinsic property and remains the same regardless of the choice of unit cell, as long as the unit cell is representative of the crystal structure.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the selection of unit cells in a crystal lattice?

answers.a: There is only one correct way to choose a unit cell for a given lattice.
answers.b: Different choices of unit cells can represent the same lattice structure.
answers.c: Non-primitive unit cells are always larger than primitive unit cells.
answers.d: Primitive unit cells cannot be used to represent complex crystal structures.

explanations.b: The same lattice structure can be represented by different choices of unit cells, including both primitive and non-primitive cells.

questions.question: Why might one choose to use a non-primitive unit cell over a primitive one?

answers.a: To simplify the visualization of the crystal structure.
answers.b: To reduce computational complexity in simulations.

explanations.a: Non-primitive unit cells are often chosen to simplify visualization and make symmetry in the crystal structure more apparent.

questions.question: Which statement about surface energy in crystals is correct?

answers.a: Surface energy depends only on the type of material, not the crystallographic orientation.
answers.b: Surface energy is higher for surfaces with higher atomic packing density.
answers.c: Surfaces with lower atomic packing density have higher surface energy.
answers.d: All crystal surfaces have the same surface energy.

explanations.c: Surfaces with lower atomic packing density tend to have higher surface energy due to more unsatisfied bonds.
